name: Computer Systems and Architecture
description: How a machine actually runs a program: binary representation, digital logic, instruction set architecture, assembly, the memory hierarchy and what determines performance.

topics.name: Data Representation
topics.summary: Everything in a computer is a bit pattern — how numbers and characters are encoded, and where the encodings break down.

subtopics.name: Binary, Hexadecimal and Conversion
subtopics.summary: Positional notation in base 2 and 16, and converting between bases.

objectives.text: Convert between decimal, binary and hexadecimal representations
Explain why hexadecimal is used as shorthand for binary
Perform binary addition and identify a carry out of the most significant bit

subtopics.name: Signed Integers and Overflow
subtopics.summary: Two's complement, the asymmetric range, and what happens when a result will not fit.

objectives.text: Represent a negative integer in two's complement and convert it back
State the range of an n-bit two's complement integer
Detect signed overflow in an addition and explain its consequence

subtopics.name: Floating-Point Numbers
subtopics.summary: Sign, exponent and mantissa, precision limits and why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3.

objectives.text: Describe the sign, exponent and mantissa fields of an IEEE 754 number
Explain why many decimal fractions cannot be represented exactly
Identify where rounding error accumulates in a computation

topics.name: Digital Logic
topics.summary: Building arithmetic and memory out of gates — the layer between physics and instructions.

subtopics.name: Boolean Algebra and Gates
subtopics.summary: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, XOR, truth tables and algebraic simplification.

objectives.text: Write the truth table of a gate network
Simplify a Boolean expression using algebraic identities or a Karnaugh map
Explain why NAND is functionally complete

subtopics.name: Combinational Circuits
subtopics.summary: Adders, multiplexers and decoders — circuits whose output depends only on current input.

objectives.text: Design a half adder and a full adder from gates
Explain the role of a multiplexer and a decoder in a datapath
Analyse propagation delay through a combinational network

subtopics.name: Sequential Circuits and State
subtopics.summary: Flip-flops, registers and clocking — how a circuit remembers.

objectives.text: Distinguish combinational from sequential logic
Describe how a D flip-flop stores a bit across a clock edge
Explain how the clock period relates to the longest combinational path

topics.name: Processor Architecture
topics.summary: The contract between hardware and software, and the machinery that honours it.

subtopics.name: Instruction Set Architecture
subtopics.summary: Instruction formats, addressing modes and the RISC/CISC distinction.

objectives.text: Describe the fields of a typical instruction encoding
Compare register, immediate and memory addressing modes
State what an ISA guarantees to a compiler writer

subtopics.name: Datapath and Control
subtopics.summary: ALU, register file, buses and the control signals that steer them.

objectives.text: Identify the datapath components used by a given instruction
Explain the role of the control unit in instruction execution
Trace data movement through the datapath for an arithmetic instruction

subtopics.name: The Instruction Execution Cycle
subtopics.summary: Fetch, decode, execute, memory access and write-back.

objectives.text: List the stages of the instruction cycle and what happens in each
Explain the role of the program counter and how branching changes it
Count the cycles a simple instruction sequence requires

topics.name: Assembly and Machine Code
topics.summary: Reading the code the processor actually executes, and how high-level constructs compile down to it.

subtopics.name: Assembly Language Basics
subtopics.summary: Registers, load/store, arithmetic and branch instructions.

objectives.text: Read a short assembly listing and state what it computes
Translate a simple arithmetic expression into assembly
Explain the load/store discipline for accessing memory

subtopics.name: Control Flow in Assembly
subtopics.summary: Conditional branches, comparisons, loops and jump targets.

objectives.text: Implement an if/else and a loop using conditional branches
Explain how condition flags are set and tested
Convert a while loop into branch-based assembly

subtopics.name: Procedures and the Stack
subtopics.summary: Calling conventions, the stack frame, arguments, return addresses and locals.

objectives.text: Describe the contents of a stack frame during a procedure call
Explain how the return address enables a call to resume correctly
State why a calling convention must be agreed between caller and callee

topics.name: The Memory Hierarchy
topics.summary: Fast memory is small and slow memory is large — caching is how the gap is hidden.

subtopics.name: Memory Technologies and Locality
subtopics.summary: Registers, SRAM, DRAM and storage, and the temporal and spatial locality caches exploit.

objectives.text: Order the levels of the memory hierarchy by speed, size and cost
Distinguish temporal from spatial locality with an example
Explain why locality makes caching effective

subtopics.name: Caches
subtopics.summary: Cache lines, direct-mapped and set-associative placement, hits, misses and replacement.

objectives.text: Compute a cache hit rate for a given access sequence
Compare direct-mapped and set-associative placement
Explain the effect of cache line size on spatial locality

subtopics.name: Writing Cache-Friendly Code
subtopics.summary: How array traversal order and data layout change real running time.

objectives.text: Explain why row-major traversal of a 2D array outperforms column-major
Identify a memory access pattern with poor locality
Estimate the effect of a cache miss on effective access time

topics.name: Performance
topics.summary: Measuring speed honestly, and the two ways architectures get faster.

subtopics.name: Measuring Performance
subtopics.summary: CPU time, clock rate, cycles per instruction and the CPU performance equation.

objectives.text: Compute CPU time from instruction count, CPI and clock rate
Explain why clock rate alone is a poor measure of performance
Compare two designs using the CPU performance equation

subtopics.name: Pipelining
subtopics.summary: Overlapping instruction stages for throughput, and the hazards that stall the pipeline.

objectives.text: Explain how pipelining improves throughput without reducing latency
Identify data, control and structural hazards in an instruction sequence
Compute the speedup of an ideal k-stage pipeline

subtopics.name: Parallelism and Amdahl's Law
subtopics.summary: Multiple cores, the limits of speedup, and where parallelism pays.

objectives.text: Apply Amdahl's law to bound the speedup from parallelising part of a program
Distinguish instruction-level from thread-level parallelism
Explain why adding cores gives diminishing returns
